Breakfast at the hotel.
Take a group excursion to the Brazilian side of the falls with an English-speaking guide.
At the meeting point of Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay, the Iguazú Falls comprise 275 immense cascades dropping from heights of 60 to 80 metres. The falls are in a national park with distinctive plant and animal life and were formed by a volcanic eruption and shifts in the Earth's layers. Their name means “big water” in Guaraní. Each cascade has its own name, and the torrents thunder into the gorge known as the Devil’s Throat. The placid flow of the Iguazú River above the falls contrasts with the churning water plunging 72 metres into the gorge. You could watch the water for hours, contemplating the scale and timelessness of the scene.

You can book an optional visit to the Bird Park (USD 50 per person) near Iguaçu National Park. Step into large aviaries where brightly coloured birds fly and walk freely among the tropical forest vegetation.

You can book the optional Macuco Safari (USD 130 per person). Travel about 3 km through the jungle in the open back of a jeep with a guide who will explain the region’s ecology. Then walk to the bank of the Iguaçu River and take a motorboat close to the falls. Expect spray, rainbows and plenty of opportunities for photographs.

Argentine side of Iguazú Falls – Buenos Aires

Breakfast at the hotel. Take a group excursion to the Argentine side of Iguazú Falls with an English-speaking guide. After the tour, transfer to the airport for your flight to Buenos Aires.
On arrival in Buenos Aires, transfer from the airport to your hotel with a driver.
